text: Moving off self-managed ClickHouse is mainly a data copy: keep the same SQL and clients
quote: Moving a self-managed ClickHouse deployment is mostly a data copy: same SQL, same clients.

text: Migration path: recreate the schema, move data through object storage, then repoint clients
quote: Recreate the schema, bridge the data through object storage, repoint, and cut the cost.

text: A migration checklist covers behaviors that change under compute-storage separation: coordinated ops, snapshot commands, settings, ingestion
quote: The focused checklist of behaviors compute–storage separation changes: centrally-coordinated operations, the storage-snapshot commands to replace, settings, and ingestion.

text: Migrations are validated by benchmarking the workload and shadowing production traffic before cutover
quote: We benchmark your workload, shadow production traffic to prove it runs in parallel, and cut over only when the numbers hold.

text: Dedicated migration engineers move customers over using proven tooling and a project plan
quote: Dedicated migration engineers move you onto ObsessionDB with proven tooling and a real project plan.

text: Supports the native ClickHouse protocol and HTTP interface, so existing ClickHouse clients and drivers connect unchanged
quote: ObsessionDB speaks the native ClickHouse protocol and HTTP interface, so every ClickHouse client and driver connects unchanged.

text: Existing queries, clients and tools work unchanged; only the host and credentials need to change
quote: every ClickHouse client and driver works against ObsessionDB unchanged. You change the host and credentials, nothing else.

text: Documentation maps what is identical to ClickHouse, what differs, what is not implemented, and what never will be
quote: An honest map of what is identical to ClickHouse, what behaves differently, what is not implemented, and what will never be implemented by design.

text: Quickstart goes from signup to a first query in about five minutes
quote: From signup to your first query in about five minutes: create a cluster, connect any ClickHouse client, load data, and query.

text: MCP server lets coding agents connect with OAuth 2.1 and no API keys, with tools to list services, run SQL and read monitoring
quote: Connect coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Zed) to your databases over MCP: OAuth 2.1, no API keys, tools to list services, run SQL, and read monitoring.

text: BI and SQL tools that support ClickHouse, such as Grafana, Metabase, Superset, Tableau and DBeaver, connect directly
quote: Any BI, dashboard, or SQL tool that connects to ClickHouse connects to ObsessionDB: Grafana, Metabase, Superset, Tableau, DBeaver, and the rest.

text: Accepts plain MergeTree DDL, with metadata in a coordination layer and data stored on object storage
quote: it takes plain MergeTree DDL on the surface, with metadata in the coordination layer and data on object storage underneath.

text: Free developer tier with a dev instance of up to 4 vCPU and 8 GB RAM, no credit card required
quote: Free developer tier. Spin up a dev instance to kick the tires. Up to 4 vCPU... No credit card required

text: CHKit provides typed commands to describe, validate, test and deploy schema and pipelines as code in CI, with reviewable diffs
quote: CHKit gives them typed commands to describe, validate, test, and deploy schema and pipelines as code: infrastructure an agent can drive, in CI, with a diff you can review.

text: Agents run on isolated, read-only compute over the same data, so they cannot slow production traffic
quote: an agent runs on isolated, read-only compute over the same data, so it can't slow your production traffic.

text: Each agent run can get its own disposable branch of production data on isolated compute over the same S3
quote: Give each agent run its own branch of production data: isolated compute over the same S3. Let it experiment for real, then throw the branch away.

text: Every agent query is logged in full, so you can replay exactly what it read down to the column
quote: Every query an agent runs is logged in full, so you can replay exactly what it read, down to the column

text: Large SQL operations run as batches of retryable tasks, with live progress and pause, retry and cancel controls
quote: Run large SQL operations as batches of retryable tasks against your service, with live progress and controls to pause, retry, or cancel while the job runs.

text: Stateless compute lets you add or remove nodes and resize without re-sharding or rebalancing
quote: Stateless compute means changing cluster shape moves no data: add or remove nodes and resize compute with no re-sharding and no rebalancing.

text: Share data with other clusters as read-only access with real-time revocable permissions, without exposing credentials or compute
quote: Share your data with other clusters... without exposing any cluster credentials or sharing its compute... read-only access with real-time revocable permissions.

text: Query monitoring offers a searchable stats table, per-execution time breakdowns, and grouped error signatures
quote: the searchable stats table, drilling down to a single execution with its time breakdown, and grouped error signatures.

text: Monitoring shows table sizes and partition shape on object storage, plus per-node CPU and memory over time
quote: table sizes and partition shape on object storage, plus per-node CPU and memory over time with selectable aggregations

text: Exposes the full stock ClickHouse observability surface and documents how to query it across the whole cluster
quote: The full ClickHouse observability surface, unchanged from stock ClickHouse, plus how to query it across the whole cluster at once

text: Any SQL query can become a monitored alert rule with an operator, threshold, interval and severity, starting from templates
quote: Turn any SQL query against your cluster into a monitored rule: set an operator, threshold, interval, and severity, start from a template

text: Reusable, organization-scoped Slack and HTTP webhook destinations can be attached to any alert rule
quote: Organization-scoped, reusable Slack and HTTP webhook destinations you set up once and attach to any rule.

text: Point-in-time recovery and time travel restore the database to any earlier moment, for example after an accidental drop
quote: Point-in-time recovery rolls you back to any moment, so an accidental drop is a quick cleanup, not an incident.

text: Daily backups are automated, with a documented recovery model that replaces manual BACKUP/RESTORE
quote: Automated daily backups, the recovery model, and why there is no manual BACKUP/RESTORE.

text: SSO login through your own identity provider, with role-based access scoped down to the table and column
quote: Log in through your own identity provider with SSO. Scope access with roles down to the table and column

text: Private networking connectivity with workloads on isolated, dedicated compute and no noisy neighbors
quote: Connect over private networking, never the public internet. Your workload runs on isolated, dedicated compute with no noisy neighbors

text: BYOC deployment keeps data inside your own cloud account or hardware
quote: In BYOC, your data never leaves your cloud or your hardware.

text: Available fully managed on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure, or as BYOC in your own AWS or Google Cloud account
quote: Run ObsessionDB fully managed on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure, or as BYOC inside your own AWS or Google Cloud account

text: Lets you compute your bill up front and compare it one-to-one against current managed ClickHouse spend
quote: Confident enough to let you compute your bill before you talk to us. Compare your current managed ClickHouse® spend, one-to-one.

text: Offers a free ClickHouse cost audit plus $3K in credits on conversion
quote: Free ClickHouse® cost audit, plus $3K in credits if you convert.

text: Cross-table partition operations re-point parts by reference, without copying row data
quote: Cross-table partition operations work by reference: the coordination layer re-points parts to the target table, so no row data is copied.

text: Supports materialized and refreshable materialized views, projections, skipping indices, and dictionaries with cross-node RELOAD
quote: Materialized views, refreshable materialized views..., projections, skipping indices (bloom_filter, minmax, set, …), dictionaries with cross-node RELOAD propagation

text: Ingestion via INSERT, the Kafka table engine, and the s3() and url() table functions works as documented
quote: INSERT, the Kafka table engine, the s3() and url() table functions, materialized views, all work as documented

text: Async inserts let the server buffer many small inserts into larger parts
quote: Use async inserts. Let the server buffer many small inserts into larger parts

text: Packed storage writes one object per part instead of one per column, roughly 15x fewer writes for wide parts
quote: ObsessionDB writes one packed object per part instead of one object per column (packed storage), on the order of 15× fewer writes for wide parts.
